newsitem.title: UK: OPTIONS - Short stg vol ticks up, gilt vol eases.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Short stg vol ticks up, gilt vol eases.

text.p: Implied volatility of short sterling options nudged higher while gilt volatility continued on its downward trajectory on Thursday, traders said.
They said the short end was eyeing next week's British budget while the long end was reluctant to move much before an upcoming U.S. Federal Reserve policy meeting.
"Gilts (vol) has been coming off quite a bit," said a broker at a French brokerage in London.

"September has been dragged down by August volatility which has been coming off quite a lot because they are predicting very little movement between now and the FOMC and they've got the July 4th holiday coming up," he said.

Brokers quoted implied volatility of September gilt options at around 6.5 percent slightly below Wednesday's levels and compared with 7.0 percent one week ago, 7.3 percent three weeks ago and 7.5 percent a month ago.
"It's on a steady decline," the broker at the French house said.
September gilt futures were quoted at 113-30, unchanged on the day.
Implied volatility of September short sterling options was quoted at 7.3 percent, up from 6.5 percent a week ago. December was quoted at 8.3 percent compared with 8.0 percent a week ago.
"It's slightly up," the broker at the French house said.

Recent strong British economic data has sparked speculation Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown will take tough measures in his budget on July 2 to dampen inflation and the Bank of England might follow with an interest rate rise.
December short sterling futures were quoted at 92.78, unchanged on the day.
The Federal Reserve Open Market Committee meets on July 1-2 with analysts divided over whether the Fed will raise rates. The Independence Day holiday follows on July 4.
Traders said volume was thin with 1,000 lots of the August 111-00 gilt puts at volatility of around 7.1 percent the main highlight.
"There's not a great deal going on," said a broker at a brokerage house on the LIFFE floor. --Jacqueline Thorpe, International Bonds Unit +44 171 542 6176
